contexts.text: I am dust and ashes = the humiliation of the human...
Under Dust, see this reference, and at AC 4293:3.
To roll themselves in ashes () = to be condemned on account of what is false.

Thou shalt make pans for the sifting of the ashes = the removing agents after uses... For ashes = such things in the natural or outward memory of man as remain after uses, and which are to be removed, lest they should stand in the way of other things following, by which again there may be uses. Explained.

The scientifics which have served for these uses are signified by the ashes that are to be removed; and the knowledges of truth and of good, through which man attains spiritual life, after they have served their use; that is, have imbued life, are signified by the ashes of the altar, which also are to be removed...
Ashes, in the opposite sense, = what is condemned, remaining after the consuming that is worked by the fire of self love.
a. [5]. Like fire in wood, under the ashes. CL 365:end.
[151a] 6. Like a shrub raised up again from its ashes... TCR 692:4.
That there was no worship whatever, is signified by the altar's being rent, and the ashes poured out ().
To gird herself with sackcloth, and roll herself in ashes () = mourning on account of the destruction of the good and truth of the Church.
To perform repentance in sackcloth and ashes () = to grieve and mourn on account of the non-reception of Divine Truth, and on account of the falsities and evils which have stood in the way.

To roll themselves in ashes () = mourning still deeper [than is signified by the putting of dust on their heads]. For ashes = what is condemned, because the fire that produces them signifies infernal love.
